To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are many studies examining the effect of nutrition and physical activity interventions on adults with or without risk factors for cardiometabolic diseases.

the literature examining interventions to maintain or improve nutrition and physical outcomes in adults with or without CVD risk is limited and there is a need for more SR of behaviour counselling or coaching provided by dietitians and/or exercise practitioners.
the majority of the literature on nutrition and physical activity interventions are focused on the general population, with a minority of studies focusing on the population with cardiometabolic risk.

there is a paucity of SR of behaviour counselling and coaching interventions for individuals who are at risk of or have a cardiometabolic condition.

there is a lack of evidence for the effect of individual nutrition and physical activity counselling/coaching provided by a dietitan/nutritionist, or exercise practitioner on the general adult population.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are several mobile applications available for nutrition and physical activity.

nutrition and physical activity interventions are available for the general population, but the evidence base for the effectiveness of nutrition and physical activity counselling or coaching provided by practitioners is lacking.

there is a need to improve the quality of research and to conduct SR to inform practice for dietitians and exercise practitioners working with individuals in the community, at work or in an outpatient setting who are healthy or with a cardiometabolic risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of nutrition and physical activity interventions that have shown to improve or maintain health outcomes in individuals with or without cardiometricablic risk.

there is a need for a SR on the effectiveness of individual level nutrition counseling or coaching from dietitian/nutritionalists and/or exercise practitioners for individuals with or without cardiomebolic risk.
there is a need for more research in the areas of behaviour counseling and coaching provided by a practitioner, and that this research is not being synthesized in SR.
